topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the fifth lecture of the cancer biology series and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer evolution, stemness, and the microenvironment.

topics.label: Clonal selection and epigenetic changes in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer evolves through the Darwinian selection of fit mutant clones and non-mutational epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchies and cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the contribution of stem cell properties, differentiation hierarchies, and specific cells of origin to tumor initiation and propagation across experimental models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, inflammation, and stromal support
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how microenvironmental factors, including chronic inflammation and supportive stromal interactions, promote tumor outgrowth and sustain established malignancies.

topics.label: Experimental and computational methods for studying tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the experimental and computational tools used to investigate tumor evolution and cellular interactions within tissues.

topics.label: Integrated multifactorial model of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how cell-of-origin properties, acquired mutations, epigenetic plasticity, and microenvironmental factors collectively drive cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming lecture on cancer therapy.
